newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Irish EU Presidency abandons potato plan.
newsitem.headline: Irish EU Presidency abandons potato plan.

text.p: The Irish EU Presidency admitted defeat on Monday in its attempt to get agreement for a so-called lightweight potato regime.
"Agreement on a potato regime will have to wait until another presidency," Irish farm minister Ivan Yates told a news conference after a farm ministers' meeting.
The statement came after ministers refused to back a compromise based on an earlier 1993 proposal.
The Irish Presidency put forward a plan similar to one agreed for the reform of the fruit and vegetable sector based on producer organisations as promoters of marketing organisations.
"A round table indication of member states' views was taken at tonight's meeting and it is clear that there is not enough support for a potato regime," said Ivan Yates.
The Netherlands takes over the EU presidency in January and an official commented, "A potato regime is not something the Dutch presidency will be enthusiastic about."
